title.label: Good app with room for improvement

content.label:
3 stars. The app does pretty much exactly what it promises — recording conversations and generating summaries — and overall it works well for that purpose. The summaries are useful, and I’ve found it helpful overall.

That said, there’s definitely room for improvement.

The biggest issue for me is the audio playback experience. There’s no good rewind or fast-forward functionality, no playback speed options, and overall the listening experience feels pretty basic. If you actually want to go back and review recordings later, those features would make a huge difference.

It also occasionally gets names wrong in the summaries/transcripts, although that’s usually a smaller issue for me compared to the audio controls.

Another frustrating issue is how sensitive it seems to internet connection changes. If your phone switches between Wi-Fi and cellular, or if the connection briefly drops, the recording can disconnect very easily. Then you have to reconnect, merge notes together, and sometimes you miss important parts of the conversation.

So overall: good app, useful concept, and it does what it says — but the audio playback tools and connection stability really need improvement.

This app has significantly improved my quality of life. I use Wave to summarize meetings for work, volunteer meetings, lessons I teach (violin/voice), rehearsals, lectures, and even medical discussions. Wave summarizes everything, turns it into plain English that anyone can understand, and separates all the topics with important points, notes, and action items. It also allows me to send recordings (from any time) and import them for the same treatment — recording in the app isn’t required. Wave recognizes voices so you can view a complete transcript later, and you can name the speakers to make reviewing the meeting easy. If there are a lot of speakers, there is sometimes confusion between the voices, but it has never negatively impacted the note summaries (which are the main product). Additionally, you can edit the summaries entirely for accuracy before exporting, and you can export to SO MANY formats, including PDF summaries that look professional enough to share, straight out of the app. On top of all this, I had a minor issue after an Apple update that changed how a feature worked, and the developer responded promptly and perfected the app very quickly. I’ve tried more than a dozen AI notes apps online because as an autistic adult and educator, it is a life-changing enhancement for me, as I would spend countless hours completing the same task on my own.
